problem_type: Standalone ESM entry uses test-runner-style assertions without an explicit canonical import
symptom: CI e2e smoke starts Electron and passes four initial checks, then aborts at the first expect with ReferenceError: expect is not defined.
direct_cause: smoke.e2e.mjs contains three active expect calls but imports neither expect nor the canonical assertion owner. Standalone Node execution does not supply a runner global.
class_root: A standalone entry must explicitly bind assertion symbols to the canonical collecting owner rather than depend on globals or direct runner imports.
affected_population: Other standalone journeys that use the same canonical expect
entry_points: CI test:e2e -> node tests/ux/smoke.e2e.mjs -> existing expect calls
core-smoke-spend-confirm.walk.mjs as a second actual standalone ownership control
internal_only_reason: The failure is a missing local ESM binding, confirmed by the exact CI log and source. The existing ./_assert.mjs export is the internal canonical collecting owner; no external runtime/library change is required.
invariants: Explicitly import expect from ./_assert.mjs in smoke, without changing any assertion or pass count
Do not declare a global expect, change ESLint globals or bypass the collecting owner with direct runner imports
New structural tests read source only; do not import or execute Electron standalone modules
Removing the actual canonical import must be rejected for both real standalone scripts
Preserve all three active smoke expect calls and reject vacuous/no-assertion inputs

door_reduction.why_not: These two actual standalone entries run distinct scenarios and must retain their own assertions. They share the existing canonical owner; adding the missing import does not remove legitimate calls. Generated with the existing mapDoors API over exactly the user-scoped smoke and actual second-standalone control, using Git base content for before and current files for after.

generality_proof: The regression checks the actual smoke and a second real core-smoke standalone. It requires a named local expect binding from the canonical owner and nonempty actual calls; virtual removal of each real import is rejected. Separate negative fixtures reject globals, comments, local stubs, wrong runner owners and a mismatched alias; an empty assertion body cannot pass. The scripts themselves are never imported or run.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Bind the standalone module's existing assertion calls to ./_assert.mjs and its collecting wrapper

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Add the missing explicit canonical import; retain the three original locator/text assertions unchanged.

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: standalone canonical expect import and calls
same_class_entry_points.evidence: Already imports expect from ./_assert.mjs. New structural regression checks its real source and removes its import only in an in-memory negative control.
Existing shared owner remains unchanged; smoke reuses it rather than a global or direct framework expect.

recurrence.reason: Runner globals can hide an omitted standalone import in any executable journey. A parser-level ownership assertion makes the same omission observable without starting an App.
same_class_scan: Read CI ci-e102-e2e-25.log 1649-1658 and smoke's exact import and three expect call sites
Read the canonical expect export and collecting wrapper in _assert.mjs
Read a second actual standalone core-smoke-spend-confirm and verified its canonical import
Initial CLI default excludes tests; used the unchanged exported mapDoors API with the two explicit standalone source files and generated real before/after maps
Separately reported other unresolved smoke symbols; did not silently expand scope or claim an end-to-end pass

prevention.invariant: Standalone expect calls have a local canonical ESM import, not an ambient runner dependency.
prevention.failure_mode: Source ownership regression rejects missing/misowned bindings before a browser/App run; the actual explicit import supplies the runtime binding.
prevention.strategy: Add one import from the already-existing canonical wrapper and directly guard its ownership with source-only negative controls.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove dependence on an undeclared ambient expect while retaining all original assertions and journey steps.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Reuse the existing assertion wrapper and existing TypeScript/Vitest structural-test pattern; no new dependency or API replacement.

migration: None; only a local standalone module binding is added. No app/project/media data is changed.
residual_risks: No App, browser, screenshot, Provider, full suite or large typecheck run; actual e2e smoke success remains coordination acceptance
Other pre-existing unresolved smoke symbols screenshotDir/screenshotSettled/electronProcess are reported and deliberately not changed under the user-limited import-only scope
The structural scope is the actual smoke plus a second real standalone control, not a claim that every unrelated journey was audited
The structural test targets canonical expect ownership, not a complete free-variable audit of every standalone symbol

The real-diff contract check retains one structural-prevention advisory because its path classifier treats executable tests/ux/smoke.e2e.mjs as test-only. The actual ESM import fixes runtime binding; no fake src artifact, scope change, checker exemption or one_off downgrade is added.
